newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen nervous, keeping eye on U.S.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen nervous, keeping eye on U.S.

text.p: A nervous German share market was expected to keep a beady eye on Wall Street and data coming out of the U.S. for the rest of the week, dealers said.

Although the fundamental outlook for German stocks was generally positive, dealers said prices were still dependent on the U.S. and said a weaker dollar against the mark would continue to put pressure on German exporting shares.

The IBIS DAX, which measures all-day trade in the DAX index of 30 leading shares, fell 14.65 points, or 0.55 percent in late trade to stand at 2,660.85 points, after German bonds suffered and Wall Street lost early gains.
Wall Street got off to a positive start after third quarter U.S. GDP rose 2.2 percent, higher than forecast, but below the previous quarter's 4.7 percent.
But the Dow and U.S. Treasuries lost ground after September new home sales dropped five percent to a higher than forecast annual rate of 816,000. The German Bund and IBIS DAX mimicked those falls.

Dealers said a continuing flow of data out of the U.S. would provide keep interest focused across the Atlantic, including U.S. jobless claims due out on Thursday and U.S. October payrolls out on Friday.
In Germany the banking sector will be at the centre of attention on Thursday, when nine month results of several banks will be published, most notably Dresdner Bank.
"After Dresdner's excellent six month results, we wonder if they can keep up the tempo," said one dealer.
